target: Mae'r opera yn adrodd stori drwy gerddoriaeth.
english: Opera tells a story through music.
tip: drwy, through, triggers soft mutation. cerddoriaeth becomes gerddoriaeth in drwy gerddoriaeth.

target: Pe bai hi heb ffonio, byddwn i wedi anghofio.
english: If she hadn't called, I would have forgotten.
tip: heb plus a verb means not having done it. heb ffonio here is hadn't called, the negative of wedi ffonio.

target: Pe bawn i'n gwybod yr ateb, byddwn i'n dweud wrthot ti.
english: If I knew the answer, I would tell you.
tip: Unreal conditions pair Pe bawn i, if I were, with byddwn i, I would. Both take the same -wn ending.

target: Pe na bawn i wedi colli'r bws, byddwn i ar amser.
english: If I hadn't missed the bus, I would have been on time.
tip: For a negative condition, add na after pe. Pe na bawn i wedi colli means if I hadn't missed.

target: Mae Branwen ferch Llŷr yn drist.
english: Branwen, daughter of Llŷr, is sad.
tip: An adjective after predicative yn soft mutates. trist becomes drist in yn drist, sad.

target: Mae'r dderwen ganmlwydd yn sefyll yng nghanol y pentref.
english: The hundred-year-old oak stands in the middle of the village.
tip: The word yn, in, triggers nasal mutation and itself becomes yng. canol turns into yng nghanol, in the middle of.

target: Mae'r stori fer yn gorffen gyda thro annisgwyl.
english: The short story ends with an unexpected twist.
tip: gyda, with, triggers aspirate mutation. tro becomes thro in gyda thro annisgwyl, with a twist.

target: Ni allwch wahanu treftadaeth oddi wrth y dirwedd a'i lluniodd.
english: One cannot separate heritage from the landscape that shaped it.
tip: After a form of gallu, can, the following verb soft mutates. gwahanu becomes wahanu in allwch wahanu.

target: Credwn i fod e'n wir.
english: I believed it was true.
tip: To report 'that it was', Welsh uses fod, from bod: Credwn i fod e'n wir = I believed it was true.

target: Trwy weithio'n galed, llwyddais i.
english: By working hard, I succeeded.
tip: Trwy before a verb-noun means 'by' doing it: Trwy weithio = by working.

target: Pa liw yw dy gar di?
english: What colour is your car?
tip: Welsh wraps 'your' around the noun: dy gar di = your car, dy before and di after gar.

target: Anfonwyd y neges at yr holl rieni trwy e-bost fore Gwener diwethaf.
english: The message was sent to all the parents by email last Friday morning.
tip: The ending -wyd makes an impersonal past passive with no named doer: Anfonwyd y neges = the message was sent.

target: Het dal ddu a siôl.
english: She wore a tall black hat and shawl.
tip: Adjectives after a feminine noun soft-mutate: after het, tal and du become dal and ddu in Het dal ddu = tall black hat.

target: Byddwn i'n hoffi dysgu hwylio.
english: I'd like to learn to sail.
tip: byddwn i means 'I would', the conditional, while bydda i means 'I will': Byddwn i'n hoffi = I would like.

target: Mae gen i lawer o negeseuon.
english: I have lots of messages.
tip: Welsh has no verb 'to have'. Possession uses mae with gen i, literally 'is with me': Mae gen i lawer = I have lots.

target: Mae dysgu yn broses gydol oes.
english: Learning is a lifelong process.
tip: A verb-noun doubles as an -ing noun: dysgu means both 'to learn' and 'learning', as in Mae dysgu = learning is.

target: Trefnodd y myfyrwyr ddigwyddiad codi arian.
english: The students organised a fundraising event.
tip: A verb's object soft-mutates: digwyddiad becomes ddigwyddiad after Trefnodd = the students organised an event.

target: Mae'r marmor yn cael ei gerfio'n gerfluniau.
english: Marble is carved into sculptures.
tip: Welsh passives use cael plus ei plus a verb-noun: cael ei gerfio = gets carved, cerfio softening to gerfio after ei.

target: Byddwn i'n mwynhau gwyliau yng nghefn gwlad.
english: I'd enjoy a holiday in the countryside.
tip: yn meaning 'in' nasal-mutates the next word and becomes yng: cefn turns into yng nghefn = in the back of.

target: Dw i erioed wedi bod yn yr Eisteddfod.
english: I have never been to the Eisteddfod.
tip: erioed means 'never' only with the perfect: Dw i erioed wedi bod = I have never been. For future 'never', use byth.

target: Os bydd hi'n bwrw glaw, arhoswn ni gartref.
english: If it rains, we'll stay at home.
tip: For a real 'if', use os with the future bydd: Os bydd hi'n bwrw glaw = if it rains. Keep pe for unreal ifs.

target: Yn yr eisteddfod y clywais i hi'n canu.
english: It was at the eisteddfod that I heard her sing.
tip: Front a phrase for emphasis, then put y before the verb: Yn yr eisteddfod y clywais i = it was there that I heard.

target: Pe bawn i wedi astudio'n galetach, byddwn i wedi pasio.
english: If I had studied harder, I would have passed.
tip: Regret about the past pairs pe bawn i wedi with byddwn i wedi: Pe bawn i wedi astudio = if I had studied harder.

target: Sut wyt ti?
english: How are you?
tip: Sut wyt ti uses ti, the familiar you for friends and family: it means how are you.
